svg.text: The first 6 prime wheels of the equator, tip to tail: the sum is Σ p^(−½−it), trace to t = 40
p = 2: radius p^(−½) = 0.707, rate ln p = 0.693 rad per unit height
p = 3: radius p^(−½) = 0.577, rate ln p = 1.099 rad per unit height
p = 5: radius p^(−½) = 0.447, rate ln p = 1.609 rad per unit height
p = 7: radius p^(−½) = 0.378, rate ln p = 1.946 rad per unit height
p = 11: radius p^(−½) = 0.302, rate ln p = 2.398 rad per unit height
p = 13: radius p^(−½) = 0.277, rate ln p = 2.565 rad per unit height
clockwise = e^(−it ln p); the mirror wheels p^(−½+it) turn the other way: together, a standing wave.
